passages.text: On the third day a wedding took place at Cana in Galilee. Jesus’ mother was there, and Jesus and His disciples had also been invited to the wedding.
passages.sermon:
A wedding took place at Cana in Galilee.
This happened on the third day.
Jesus’ mother was at the wedding.
People invited Jesus to the wedding.
People also invited Jesus’ disciples to the wedding.
passages.original: Καὶ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ γάμος ἐγένετο ἐν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἦν ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐκεῖ ἐκλήθη δὲ καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν γάμον

passages.text: When the wine ran out, Jesus’ mother said to Him, “They have no more wine.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus attended a wedding in Cana of Galilee.
His mother was also there.
Jesus’ disciples were present.
The people at the wedding ran out of wine.
Jesus’ mother noticed this problem.
She spoke to Jesus.
She said, “They have no more wine.”
passages.original: καὶ ὑστερήσαντος οἴνου λέγει ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ πρὸς αὐτόν Οἶνον οὐκ ἔχουσιν

passages.text: “Woman, why does this concern us?” Jesus replied. “My hour has not yet come.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His mother.\r\nHe said, “Woman, why does this concern us?”\r\nHe said, “My hour has not yet come.”
passages.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί γύναι οὔπω ἥκει ἡ ὥρα μου

passages.text: His mother said to the servants, “Do whatever He tells you.”
passages.sermon: Mary was the mother of Jesus.\r\nShe spoke to the servants.\r\nShe said, “Do whatever Jesus tells you.”
passages.original: Λέγει ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ τοῖς διακόνοις Ὅ τι ἂν λέγῃ ὑμῖν ποιήσατε

passages.text: Now six stone water jars had been set there for the Jewish rites of purification. Each could hold from twenty to thirty gallons.
passages.sermon:
Six stone water jars stood there.
People used these jars for Jewish purification rituals.
Each jar could hold about twenty gallons.
Some jars could hold up to thirty gallons.
passages.original: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐκεῖ λίθιναι ὑδρίαι ἓξ κατὰ τὸν καθαρισμὸν τῶν Ἰουδαίων κείμεναι χωροῦσαι ἀνὰ μετρητὰς δύο ἢ τρεῖς

passages.text: Jesus told the servants, “Fill the jars with water.” So they filled them to the brim.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was at a wedding in Cana of Galilee.
His mother was there.
His disciples were there.
There were six large stone water jars.
These jars were used for Jewish purification rites.
Each jar could hold twenty to thirty gallons.
Jesus spoke to the servants.
He said, “Fill the jars with water.”
The servants obeyed Jesus.
They filled the jars to the brim.
passages.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Γεμίσατε τὰς ὑδρίας ὕδατος Καὶ ἐγέμισαν αὐτὰς ἕως ἄνω

passages.text: “Now draw some out,” He said, “and take it to the master of the banquet.” They did so, and the master of the banquet tasted the water that had been turned into wine. He did not know where it was from, but the servants who had drawn the water knew. Then he called the bridegroom aside and said, “Everyone serves the fine wine first, and then the cheap wine after the guests are drunk. But you have saved the fine wine until now!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the servants.
He said, “Now draw some out and take it to the master of the banquet.”
The servants obeyed Jesus.
They took some to the master of the banquet.
The master of the banquet tasted the water.
The water had become wine.
The master of the banquet did not know where the wine came from.
The servants who had drawn the water knew where it came from.
The master of the banquet called the bridegroom aside.
He spoke to the bridegroom.
He said, “Everyone serves the fine wine first.
After the guests have drunk freely, they serve the cheaper wine.
But you have saved the fine wine until now.”
passages.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἀντλήσατε νῦν καὶ φέρετε τῷ ἀρχιτρικλίνῳ Οἱ δὲ ἤνεγκαν ὡς δὲ ἐγεύσατο ὁ ἀρχιτρίκλινος τὸ ὕδωρ οἶνον γεγενημένον καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει πόθεν ἐστίν οἱ δὲ διάκονοι ᾔδεισαν οἱ ἠντληκότες τὸ ὕδωρ φωνεῖ τὸν νυμφίον ὁ ἀρχιτρίκλινος καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Πᾶς ἄνθρωπος πρῶτον τὸν καλὸν οἶνον τίθησιν καὶ ὅταν μεθυσθῶσιν τὸν ἐλάσσω σὺ τετήρηκας τὸν καλὸν οἶνον ἕως ἄρτι

passages.text: Jesus performed this, the first of His signs, at Cana in Galilee. He thus revealed His glory, and His disciples believed in Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus performed a miracle at Cana in Galilee.
This was the first sign Jesus did.
Jesus showed His glory by this sign.
His disciples saw what He did.
His disciples believed in Him.
passages.original: Ταύτην ἐποίησεν ἀρχὴν τῶν σημείων ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἐφανέρωσεν τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: After this, He went down to Capernaum with His mother and brothers and His disciples, and they stayed there a few days.
passages.sermon:
Jesus went to Capernaum.
His mother went with Him.
His brothers went with Him.
His disciples went with Him.
They all went together.
They stayed in Capernaum for a few days.
passages.original: Μετὰ τοῦτο κατέβη εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ αὐτὸς καὶ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκεῖ ἔμειναν οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας

passages.text: When the Jewish Passover was near, Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon: Jesus is the Son of God.\r\nThe Jewish Passover was near.\r\nJesus went up to Jerusalem.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγγὺς ἦν τὸ πάσχα τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ ἀνέβη εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ὁ Ἰησοῦς

passages.text: In the temple courts He found men selling cattle, sheep, and doves, and money changers seated at their tables.
passages.sermon:
Jesus entered the temple courts.
He saw men selling cattle.
He saw men selling sheep.
He saw men selling doves.
He saw money changers sitting at their tables.
passages.original: καὶ εὗρεν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τοὺς πωλοῦντας βόας καὶ πρόβατα καὶ περιστερὰς καὶ τοὺς κερματιστὰς καθημένους

passages.text: So He made a whip out of cords and drove all from the temple courts, both sheep and cattle. He poured out the coins of the money changers and overturned their tables.
passages.sermon:
Jesus entered the temple courts.
He saw people selling animals there.
He made a whip from cords.
He used the whip to drive everyone out of the temple courts.
He drove out the sheep and the cattle.
He poured out the coins of the money changers.
He overturned the tables of the money changers.
passages.original: καὶ ποιήσας φραγέλλιον ἐκ σχοινίων πάντας ἐξέβαλεν ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ τά τε πρόβατα καὶ τοὺς βόας καὶ τῶν κολλυβιστῶν ἐξέχεεν τὰ κέρματα καὶ τὰς τραπέζας ἀνέτρεψεν

passages.text: To those selling doves He said, “Get these out of here! How dare you turn My Father’s house into a marketplace!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw people selling doves in the temple.
He spoke to those selling doves.
He said, "Take these things away from here."
He said, "Do not make my Father's house a house of trade."
He called the temple His Father's house.
He told them not to turn it into a marketplace.
passages.original: καὶ τοῖς τὰς περιστερὰς πωλοῦσιν εἶπεν Ἄρατε ταῦτα ἐντεῦθεν μὴ ποιεῖτε τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Πατρός μου οἶκον ἐμπορίου

passages.text: His disciples remembered that it is written: “Zeal for Your house will consume Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus had disciples.
His disciples saw what He did in the temple.
They remembered a scripture.
The scripture says, “Zeal for Your house will consume Me.”
passages.original: Ἐμνήσθησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι γεγραμμένον ἐστίν Ὁ ζῆλος τοῦ οἴκου σου καταφάγεταί με

passages.text: On account of this, the Jews demanded, “What sign can You show us to prove Your authority to do these things?”
passages.sermon:
The Jews saw what Jesus did in the temple.
They spoke to Jesus.
They asked Him a question.
They said, “What sign can you show us?”
They wanted proof of His authority.
They wanted to know why He did these things.
They demanded a sign to show He had the right to act this way.
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθησαν οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Τί σημεῖον δεικνύεις ἡμῖν ὅτι ταῦτα ποιεῖς

passages.text: Jesus answered, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up again.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Jews.
He answered their question.
He said, “Destroy this temple.
In three days I will raise it up again.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν

passages.text: “This temple took forty-six years to build,” the Jews replied, “and You are going to raise it up in three days?”
passages.sermon: The Jews spoke to Jesus.\r\nThey said, “This temple took forty-six years to build.”\r\nThey asked, “Can you raise it up in three days?”
passages.original: Εἶπαν οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι Τεσσεράκοντα καὶ ἓξ ἔτεσιν οἰκοδομήθη ὁ ναὸς οὗτος καὶ σὺ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερεῖς αὐτόν

passages.text: But Jesus was speaking about the temple of His body.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was speaking about His own body.
He called His body a temple.
He did not mean the building in Jerusalem.
He used the word "temple" to describe Himself.
passages.original: Ἐκεῖνος δὲ ἔλεγεν περὶ τοῦ ναοῦ τοῦ σώματος αὐτοῦ

passages.text: After He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had said this. Then they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.
passages.sermon:
Jesus rose from the dead.
His disciples remembered His words.
They remembered that Jesus had said this before.
They believed the Scripture.
They believed the word Jesus had spoken.
passages.original: ὅτε οὖν ἠγέρθη ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐμνήσθησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι τοῦτο ἔλεγεν καὶ ἐπίστευσαν τῇ γραφῇ καὶ τῷ λόγῳ ὃν εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς

passages.text: While He was in Jerusalem at the Passover Feast, many people saw the signs He was doing and believed in His name.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in Jerusalem.
It was the time of the Passover Feast.
Many people saw the signs Jesus was doing.
These people believed in His name.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἦν ἐν τοῖς Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν τῷ πάσχα ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ θεωροῦντες αὐτοῦ τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐποίει

passages.text: But Jesus did not entrust Himself to them, for He knew them all.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in Jerusalem at the Passover Feast.
Many people saw the signs Jesus did.
Many people believed in Jesus’ name.
Jesus did not entrust Himself to these people.
Jesus knew all people.
Jesus understood everyone.
passages.original: αὐτὸς δὲ Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἐπίστευεν αὑτὸν αὐτοῖς διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν γινώσκειν πάντας

passages.text: He did not need any testimony about man, for He knew what was in a man.
passages.sermon: Jesus did not need anyone to tell Him about people.\r\nJesus already knew what was inside each person.
passages.original: καὶ ὅτι οὐ χρείαν εἶχεν ἵνα τις μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου αὐτὸς γὰρ ἐγίνωσκεν τί ἦν ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ
